subject: medicine
title: Pleural diseases and pneumothorax

steps.tx: Suspect pleural effusion when one base is **stony dull** with absent breath sounds, shifting the **mediastinum** away when large. Expect the chest film to show a **meniscus sign** with a blunted costophrenic angle, and use ultrasound to spot septations and guide tapping. Send fluid for pH, culture, protein and LDH to apply Light criteria, and separate transudates in heart failure from exudates in TB, malignancy, pneumonia, embolism and pancreatitis.
steps.say: Suspect pleural effusion when one lung base sounds stony dull with absent breath sounds, shifting the mediastinum away when large. Expect the chest film to show a curved meniscus with a blunted costophrenic angle, and use ultrasound to spot septations and guide tapping. Send the fluid for pH, culture, protein and LDH to apply Light criteria, and separate transudates in heart failure from exudates in tuberculosis, malignancy, pneumonia, embolism and pancreatitis.

steps.tx: This frontal chest radiograph shows a large homogeneous **pleural effusion** filling the left base with a concave upper **meniscus sign**. Note the blunted costophrenic angle and the **mediastinal shift** pushing structures to the opposite side. Learn these signs because the exam loves asking which side the trachea moves in a large effusion.
steps.say: Look at this frontal chest radiograph because it shows a large pleural effusion filling the left base. The upper edge curves upward in a concave meniscus while the costophrenic angle looks blunted and full. Note how the mediastinum shifts toward the opposite side under pressure from the fluid. Learn these signs well because the exam loves asking which way the trachea moves in a large effusion.

steps.tx: Suspect **pneumothorax** when sudden pleuritic pain with breathlessness strikes a tall thin young patient. Expect a **hyperresonant** note with silent breath sounds, and fear **tension physiology** with tracheal shift away and shock. Confirm it with a visible visceral pleural edge on film, separate primary blebs from secondary COPD bullae, decompress tension at once through the second interspace, and drain with a Seldinger chest tube without ever clamping it.
steps.say: Suspect pneumothorax when sudden sharp chest pain with breathlessness strikes a tall thin young patient. Expect an overly resonant note with silent breath sounds, and fear tension physiology with tracheal shift away and shock. Confirm the diagnosis with a visible pleural edge on the film, separate primary blebs from secondary bullae in lung disease, decompress tension at once through the second interspace, and drain the chest with a Seldinger tube without ever clamping it.

steps.tx: Suspect **mesothelioma** decades after asbestos exposure, often with a thirty year lag, when chest pain and weight loss accompany a nodular pleural rind. Confirm it with **VATS biopsy** and immunohistochemistry, and note calcified bilateral diaphragmatic **pleural plaques** as markers of exposure. Treat with pemetrexed based chemotherapy, arrange compensation claims for industrial disease, palliate pain and breathlessness, and watch exposed workers while separating benign plaques and fibrotic asbestosis.
steps.say: Suspect mesothelioma decades after asbestos exposure, often with a lag of thirty years, when chest pain and weight loss accompany a nodular pleural rind. Confirm the diagnosis with keyhole biopsy and special stains, and note calcified plaques on both sides of the diaphragm as markers of exposure. Treat the disease with pemetrexed based chemotherapy, arrange compensation claims for industrial disease, palliate pain and breathlessness, and watch exposed workers while separating benign plaques and fibrotic lung stiffness.

steps.tx: Diagnose **empyema** when fever with low pleural pH and glucose complicates pneumonia, and use **ultrasound** to spot loculations and septations. Drain it with a small bore **pigtail catheter**, break loculations with fibrinolytics, and refer for VATS surgery with decortication when drugs fail. Give prolonged antibiotics guided by cultures, watch for empyema necessitatis bursting through the wall, follow films until the lung expands, and separate milky chylothorax and bloody haemothorax.
steps.say: Diagnose empyema when fever with acidic low glucose fluid complicates pneumonia, and use ultrasound to spot loculations and septations. Drain the chest with a small bore pigtail catheter, break loculations with clot dissolving drugs, and refer for keyhole surgery that peels the rind when drugs fail. Give prolonged antibiotics guided by cultures, watch for pus bursting through the chest wall, follow films until the lung expands, and separate milky chyle leak and bloody traumatic collections.
